title: Make Rust path/persistence fixtures portable across Unix and WSL
outcome:
The required Rust gate was first invoked through WSL because PowerShell treated scripts/test-rust.sh as a non-executing file association. WSL ran 1,733 tests and exposed two test portability defects, while both focused tests pass through Git-for-Windows Bash against the native Windows Cargo toolchain.

1. tests::project_creation_races::remote_session_create_publishes_prior_dirty_localization_recovery removes a fake database directory beneath std::env::temp_dir(), then persistence hardening attempts to chmod that path's parent. Under WSL the parent is root-owned /tmp, producing EPERM. The fixture must restore to a user-owned temp directory/file, never make /tmp itself the permission-hardening target.
2. tests::projects::rejects_session_workdirs_outside_the_selected_project hard-codes /tmp and /Users. On Linux/WSL /Users is absent, so it returns '`/Users` is not a directory' before exercising containment. Build both existing project/outside directories under a temp root.

Acceptance: both focused tests and the complete scripts/test-rust.sh gate pass under a supported Unix environment as well as native Windows; fixtures must not attempt chmod on a shared system temp root.
